In the legs I playtested, I chose how to get to the airport, then the simulator showed me an itinerary it had already picked. That’s a natural place to add one meaningful decision without redesigning the game. I’d start with an optional manual flight booking setting. When you reach the airport, you’d see up to three distinct itineraries with their departure time, landing time, connections, and any known delays. You could grab the earliest arrival or take a direct flight that lands a little later. Auto-booking would stay the default, and we could test the feature on one airport leg before expanding it. If you’d rather do a smaller update first, I’d fix the Race Traffic panel when you’re ready to revisit those bugs. Seeing rivals arrive or depart before it actually happens gives away information that would matter even more once you can choose your own flight. let's think more generally, give suggestions for things we coukd change/add/remove for the future I’d focus future updates on making legs feel different from each other. The simulator already has a lot of season settings and detailed results. The bigger opportunity is to make the route itself change how you race. # Idea What it would change 1 Give legs distinct structures A city sprint with short transfers, a rural leg where one long ride matters, or an overnight leg where a venue opening brings teams back together. Mix up the order of tasks and travel so the next clue feels less predictable. 2 Make Detours feel like actual choices Give both options names and a short clue about what they involve. One might reward navigation and the other dexterity, so the better choice depends on your team. Keep Safe/Risky as one kind of Detour. 3 Make transport fit the location Offer a ferry where there’s a water crossing, a metro where it makes sense, and a taxi where speed is worth paying for. I’d start by trimming the combinations that make travel feel interchangeable between cities. 4 Add manual flight booking Let players choose between a few meaningful itineraries, with auto-booking available. This could make the airport the main decision of some legs. 5 Reveal the destination through the first clue Let the Leg Start screen show the departure order and cash, then reveal the destination when you open the clue. Custom routes could still be visible in setup. 6 Add a season route builder Build on the existing route editor by letting players choose a leg structure for each city and save the route as a reusable preset. For random non-eliminations, the route could draw extra cities from a reserve list. 7 Make Roadblock skills easier to manage Show which skills are still available and give a short hint about the task before you commit. Using your strongest skill now should feel like a decision you’ll remember later. 8 Give the finale its own format Bring back clues from earlier legs in a final memory task, or have teams reconstruct part of their route. A season-long payoff would make the finish feel different from a regular elimination leg. 9 Show where you gained or lost ground Put one or two turning points at the top of the recap, like “You gained three places at the Detour” or “Your connection cost you 42 minutes.” Keep the full charts available to open. 10 Trim repeated information during play Keep the current clue, time, cash, and available choices easy to find. Fold away empty traffic sections and repeated route details so the next decision is clear. My pick for the next update is distinct leg structures. I’d prototype two using the mechanics you already have: a city sprint where task choices drive the standings and an overnight leg where reaching a venue before it opens can erase an early lead. Those two would tell us how much variety we can get out of the current simulator before we add more systems. I like suggestion 5 add that Added Open Clue to the Leg Start screen. No ZIP to extract. next up look at the sim and look and what looks so "ai" about it and just looks like it easnt human made and tell me. i want this sim to not feel ai and i dont want u to make it like u do all the other basic websites you make it because they give vibecoded and AI so much and i dont like that The most “AI” thing about the sim is how often it decorates information without deciding what matters most. I opened your latest build and played through the first leg. The home screen already has a personality. I’d keep the big Amazing Race title, the postcard art, and the playful colors. The problem gets more noticeable once you start racing. Where I noticed it What gives it that feel Season setup Almost every setting has a colored border, inside another colored panel, under a row of colored navigation pills. Starting Cash and an advanced timing setting look equally important. It feels like every field was styled individually before anyone looked at the whole screen. Choose Your Team In my desktop render, Team 1 wrapped as “Tea / m 1” inside a wide, mostly empty card. The tiny team-color square sits by itself in the middle. This is the strongest tell for me. The card has room for the name, but the decoration got the better spot. Team skills Every skill gets a striped ticket, colored border, progress bar, and number badge. The bar and number communicate the same value. Across 15 skills, it’s harder to spot what your team is actually good at. First clue and Pit Stop I’d change my own first-clue implementation here. “Race to Bangalore, India” is the big reveal, but it sits in a shallow full-width panel that looks like another settings box. Pit Stop has the same problem. Nandi Hills is a great specific location, and the screen gives it a long cream rectangle with a small check-in button underneath. Both moments deserve a clearer focal point. Transport and flights In the transport screen I saw, an almost-empty traffic panel took up more room than the choices. On the flight screen, the route and times appear across several rows of cards before you get to the itinerary. A real departure board is a better reference for this screen because it puts the information you compare in one place. Results The standings are one of the most race-specific parts of the sim. But on a wide screen, the team name hugs the left edge and its time sits all the way on the right. Every row gets its own treatment, so the winner, your team, and the elimination compete with the rest of the table. I’d keep the color and the travel theme. I’d get stricter about where each belongs. Use the airmail stripe on the title screen and clue envelopes, where it has a purpose. Use team colors to follow teams through departure order, traffic, and placements. Give setup fields a quieter treatment so you can scan them. And use the actual route, clue, and standings to give the gameplay screens their character. My first design pass would be Choose Your Team and the first clue. Fix the obvious name-wrap problem, then make opening a clue feel like a race moment. Those are two small screens where we can agree on what feels like your sim before touching the rest. The Amazing Race
